summary: Identified critical failure masking in runOne, file handle leak in openJob, unhandled promise rejections in startHeartbeat, and missing input sanitization for file paths.

findings.title: Failure masking in runOne catch block
findings.body: In runOne, the catch block catches all errors and returns { id, ok: true }. This silently masks any failure during file opening or writing and falsely reports successful job execution to the caller.
findings.recommendation: Update the catch block to return { id, ok: false, error: err.message } or rethrow the error so failures can be detected by callers.

findings.title: File descriptor leak in openJob on size limit validation
findings.body: In openJob, if stat.size exceeds 1,000,000 bytes, an error is thrown without closing the opened file handle or removing it from the handles map, resulting in leaked file descriptors and retained references.
findings.recommendation: Call await handle.close() and handles.delete(id) before throwing the error when the log file exceeds the maximum permitted size.

findings.title: Unhandled promise rejection and unmanaged timer in startHeartbeat
findings.body: startHeartbeat calls asynchronous fs.appendFile inside setInterval without handling promise rejections. Any I/O error (such as permission errors or full disk) will trigger an unhandled promise rejection that can terminate the Node.js process. Additionally, the timer ID is not returned, preventing cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Attach a .catch() handler to fs.appendFile to log or handle write errors, and return the interval timer ID so the caller can clear the interval.

findings.title: Path traversal vulnerability via unsanitized job ID
findings.body: The id parameter is interpolated directly into filesystem paths in openJob and startHeartbeat without validation or sanitization. If an untrusted ID containing path traversal characters (such as '../') is passed, operations may read or write outside /var/jobs/.
findings.recommendation: Validate id against an expected format (such as /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/) or use path.basename before constructing file paths.

samples.summary: The queue implementation masks job failures as successes, leaks file descriptors when size limits are exceeded, and produces unhandled promise rejections in heartbeat timers.

findings.title: Catch block reports false success on job failure
findings.body: In `runOne`, the catch block returns `{ id, ok: true }` when `openJob` or `handle.write` throws. This masks all failures and incorrectly informs callers that the job succeeded.
findings.recommendation: Return `{ id, ok: false, error }` or propagate the error in the catch block.

findings.title: Unclosed file handle leak when log exceeds size limit
findings.body: In `openJob`, if `stat.size` exceeds 1,000,000 bytes, an Error is thrown without closing the opened `handle` or deleting it from `handles`, leaking file descriptors over time.
findings.recommendation: Call `await handle.close()` and remove `id` from `handles` before throwing the error.

findings.title: Unhandled promise rejection in heartbeat interval
findings.body: In `startHeartbeat`, the promise returned by `fs.appendFile` is not awaited or caught inside `setInterval`. Any filesystem failure will cause an unhandled promise rejection.
findings.recommendation: Attach a `.catch()` handler to `fs.appendFile` and return the interval ID so the heartbeat can be cleared.

samples.summary: Identified error swallowing masking job failures, file descriptor leaks on oversized logs and completed jobs, and unhandled promise rejections in the heartbeat timer.

findings.title: Error swallowed and falsely reported as success in runOne
findings.body: In `runOne`, the catch block catches failures from `openJob` or `handle.write` and returns `{ id, ok: true }`. This causes job failures (e.g., oversized logs or file access errors) to be silently reported as successful executions.
findings.recommendation: Return `{ id, ok: false, error }` in the catch block or allow the error to propagate.

findings.title: File descriptor leak when log size threshold is exceeded in openJob
findings.body: In `openJob`, `fs.open` creates a FileHandle and stores it in `handles`. When `stat.size > 1_000_000`, an Error is thrown without closing `handle` or removing it from the `handles` Map, causing an unclosed file descriptor leak.
findings.recommendation: Ensure `await handle.close()` is called and the entry is deleted from `handles` before throwing the error.

findings.title: Unhandled promise rejection and untracked timer in startHeartbeat
findings.body: `startHeartbeat` invokes `fs.appendFile` (from `node:fs/promises`) inside `setInterval` without awaiting or attaching a `.catch()` handler. Any write failure (e.g., disk full or permission error) will trigger an unhandled promise rejection. Additionally, the timer ID is not returned, preventing the heartbeat from being stopped.
findings.recommendation: Attach a `.catch()` error handler to `fs.appendFile` inside the interval callback, and return the timer handle from `startHeartbeat` so callers can clear it.

findings.title: Unclosed FileHandle across job execution lifecycle
findings.body: `runOne` opens a FileHandle via `openJob` and writes to it, but never closes the handle upon job completion or failure, leading to accumulating open file descriptors over time.
findings.recommendation: Close the FileHandle in a `finally` block or provide an explicit cleanup/close lifecycle function.
